input.quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: I searched the full agreement for audit, inspection, verification, records, books, monitoring and access rights and found no provision entitling TrueLink to audit, inspect or verify Client's usage, records or systems. Section 5/6 runs the other way: it gives Client (not the Vendor) the right to supporting documentation and to contest charges, and Section 2(e) gives Client real-time access to its own usage statistics and raw log files. Section 8(f) lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms against spamming, but that is an operational control on the hosted Interface, not an audit right over Client's systems or records. Since no audit obligation binds us, there is nothing exceeding the preferred position (no more than annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access) and no reason to introduce audit rights against ourselves. No redline proposed.
